deepdive.sec: Diversified retail NBFC — gold loans + MSME/LAP + affordable housing + construction finance, with fee engines in insurance distribution and car-loan distribution

bull_bear.body:
- **Capital is being steered deliberately into gold at the expense of MSME growth** — the single clearest capital-allocation statement on the call: "all the allocation of capital was towards the gold loan segment and keeping the overall growth in the range of about 50% to 60% annually, we have kept the gold loan on a higher priority."
- **Leverage 3.7x with CAR 24.7% (NBFC) / 27.8% (HFC)** — "providing headroom to support growth across business segments." No capital raise, buyback, or dividend was discussed on the call; no question was asked on capital return.
- **Liability diversification is the active programme:** 40+ lender relationships (5 added in Q1), NCD/CP at ~10% of mix, public bond issuance, institutional refinancing, and a **USD 1bn GMTN** shelf established for offshore dollar access.
- **Liquidity buffer INR 4,037 crores** across cash, bank balances, investments and undrawn lines, against a book growing 62% YoY.
- **Provisioning is being used as a buffer, not just a rule:** CF PCR lifted to 70% and consolidated PCR to 43.3% "in-line with our prudent provisioning policy… and keeping buffer for evolving macroeconomic conditions in the form of **management overlay**."
- **Capital-efficiency lever:** co-lending/DA at 20% of AUM is explicitly framed as "our strategy of **capital-efficient growth**" — which makes the CLM1-driven stall a capital-efficiency problem, not only a fee problem.
- **Discipline stated on the fee business:** "we follow the unit economics. So, at the cost of profitability, we are not increasing the volume. There are some players who do the cash burn and grow their volume, but we are following a philosophy **not to do the cash burn**."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
1. **Gold concentration is now the company.** Gold is ~48% of AUM heading to a guided ~55%, contributed the entire Stage-2 increase (INR 373 cr of INR 385 cr), and its yield (~18.5%) is what carries blended spread. Management's own hedge is explicit: "**The further fall in the gold prices might affect a growth**."
2. **Stage-2 coverage question went unanswered.** The analyst asked "why is the coverage being cut from 11.8% to 9.4%, while the pool grew… What changed in the last estimate?" — the reply addressed only the segment split. **Unresolved on this transcript.**
3. **400 branches in two quarters after a zero-add Q1.** The most checkable near-term commitment on the call, hard-dated "on or before December 2026," with the Q2 leg at ~150.
4. **Co-lending regulatory transition.** "Co-lending volume slowed down during the quarter to 4% growth quarter-on-quarter on account of **new co-lending guidelines** coming into effect and requirement of partner banks to **move to CLM1 model**. Of our 11 partners, **6 banks have already moved**" — 5 still to migrate, income already −8% YoY on a line that is 20% of AUM.
5. **Cost of funds has no further tailwind by management's own admission** ("we don't see much scope in the cost of fund reduction from this level"), while cost-to-income improvement is also guided to stop at 44–45%. Both margin levers are being called out as exhausted at the same time.
6. **Asset quality is guided flat, not better:** "We don't see any reduction from here" on 1.1% GNPA / 0.6% NNPA.
7. **Construction finance is lumpy and single-name sensitive** — one account moved segment GNPA 0.3% → 0.7%. Plus **INR 125 cr under DCCO extension held outside GNPA** as standard.
8. **Monsoon cuts both ways for gold demand.** "if the monsoon is weaker, some of the micro finance and marginal farmer will go for the requirement to meet their cash gaps by way of acquiring gold loans" — i.e. a *strong* monsoon is a demand headwind for the gold book.
9. **Leadership churn is a live investor concern**, raised twice and pressed ("in the last couple of years, we have seen multiple CEOs churning up and still the position is vacant"). See §11 for the response.
10. **Macro backdrop flagged by management itself:** "Uncertain global geopolitical situation, energy security, oil & gold price volatility, rupee depreciation and volatile capital markets led to overall macro environment being soft for the quarter."
11. **Disclosure gap:** product-wise disbursement breakup declined on the call ("we will give you these data offline").
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- **Confident, numbers-forward, and willing to raise guidance in a soft macro quarter** — the AUM target was revised up twice (opening and closing remarks), which is an unusual level of commitment to repeat.
- **Handled the leadership-churn challenge with a structural explanation rather than deflection.** Named tenures for each business head: gold loans "has been with us since the day we started," construction finance "almost about more than 9 years," housing "almost 10 years," MSME's prior head "about 7 years," credit head Vaibhav Shah "more than 7-8 years," CRO Sanjeev Srivastava "almost 3 years back." Key reframe: "Our Head of Internal Audit, CCO and CFO had to move to HFC, when our housing subsidiary achieved scale of **INR5,000 crores AUM** and also going by the **RBI regulation**, we must have a separate CCO and CFO in the housing finance. So, we have internally transferred from current NBFC to the HFC… **So, it is not that they moved out.**" Normalised the residual: "it is quite normal that 10%-20% churning in leadership happens."
- **Flat, unhedged answer on the CEO question** — asked when a long-term CEO would arrive, the reply was: "**There's no CEO position vacant. And there is no plan to bring any CEO.**" Decisive, and worth holding against the promoter-MD-centric structure.
- **Candid on the limits of its own margin story** — voluntarily closed off further cost-of-funds and cost-to-income improvement rather than leaving optimistic room, and guided asset quality flat ("We don't see any reduction from here").
- **Explicit about growth-versus-profit philosophy** in the fee business: "we are not growing the book only because of the — for the sake of numbers… Growth has to be along with profit."
- **Weak points:** the Stage-2 coverage question was left unanswered; product-wise disbursement was pushed offline; and the technology section, while quantified, ran long relative to the Q&A time available (the call was cut for "time constraint" after nine questioners).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
1. **The Q1 branch pause was the point, not a miss.** Holding gold branches at exactly 1,000 after 196 FY26 adds converted vintage into measurable productivity — INR 17 cr → INR 19 cr per branch and INR 1.8 cr → INR 3.4 cr AUM per employee — and that, more than any pricing action, is what moved cost-to-income 44.2% from 49.4%. It also means the 400-branch Q2–Q3 push will *dilute* those productivity metrics before it adds to them.
2. **Rising Stage 2 alongside a falling gold GNPA is internally consistent, not contradictory.** Gold Stage-2 rises mechanically with LTV breaches when prices fall; the automated margin-call/auction mechanism at 85% LTV is what keeps it from becoming Stage 3. The tell to watch is whether Stage 2 *drains back* when gold recovers — if it converts instead, the moat claim fails.
3. **A strong monsoon is a headwind for this book.** Management said it plainly in reverse: weak monsoon pushes marginal farmers and MFI borrowers into gold loans. Most rural-lending read-throughs run the other way — CGCL's gold engine is counter-cyclical to rural cash flows.
4. **The co-lending stall is a capital-efficiency issue disguised as a fee issue.** Co-lending/DA is 20% of AUM and explicitly the "capital-efficient growth" lever; with 5 of 11 partner banks still un-migrated to CLM1, the DA/PTC workaround is now load-bearing — and it works only because the book is gold-heavy and PSL-eligible.
5. **Both margin levers were closed on the same call.** Management guided cost of funds to no further improvement in FY27 *and* cost-to-income to stop at 44–45%. That leaves the entire FY28 ROAE 19–21% / ROAA 4.2–4.7% commitment resting on **asset-side mix** (gold to ~55%, yield +50–75 bps) and **volume**, with no cushion if gold growth slows.
6. **The RBI-mandated HFC officer separation explains away much of the "churn" narrative** — three senior exits (Internal Audit head, CCO, CFO) were internal transfers forced by the housing subsidiary crossing INR 5,000 cr AUM. That is a growth *consequence* being read by the market as an instability signal.
7. **The AI disclosure is unusually falsifiable for a mid-cap NBFC** — it is stated as throughput and coverage (6.7 lakh calls, 2.64 lakh geo-tagged visits, 166→529 msgs/min, 70mn API calls/month, 90%/93% digital collections) rather than as capability, which makes it checkable next quarter. The OpenAI tie-up, by contrast, is explicitly still at "we will explore" stage — the two should not be conflated.
8. **Yield is being bought with smaller tickets, and the incentive plan was changed to enforce it** — a deliberate structural choice that raises servicing cost per rupee and makes the branch/productivity build a prerequisite, not a parallel initiative.
9. **INR 125 cr of DCCO-extension exposure sits outside GNPA as standard.** It surfaced only because an analyst asked. Reported construction-finance asset quality should be read with it alongside.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Equity: "Strengthened Capital Adequacy through infusion of ₹20bn equity capital in Q1FY26 via QIP"; the journey timeline also marks earlier capital-raising events of a ₹4.5 bn QIP and a ₹14.4 bn Rights Issue.
- Capital position at Q1 FY27: net worth ₹76 bn (the ownership slide separately shows consolidated net worth ₹75.7bn as of Jun'26, "Not adjusted for DTAs"), borrowings ₹276 bn, D/E 3.7x and CRAR 24.7% on a standalone basis (CGHFL CRAR 27.8%).
- Liability strategy is diversification-led: "Relationship with 40+ Lenders" with 5 new lenders added in Q1 FY27, ₹12,710 mn raised through NCDs and CPs in Q1 FY27, new bank sanctions of ₹110 Bn in FY26 and ₹38,680 mn in Q1 FY27, and a stated plan to "raise NCD/CP; widen lender base; reduce cost of funds"; the ALM slide states maturity risk "No" with cumulative net inflow across all buckets.
- Co-lending is framed explicitly as capital allocation: "Additional source of funds while conserving capital and boost RoE" and "Diversification of borrowings", with the funding-mix slide showing Co-lending/DA at 24% of the ₹358 bn total funding at Q1 FY27.
- Credit ratings: "Secured 'Ba3' rating with Stable Outlook from Moody's Ratings and 'BB- Stable' rating from Fitch Ratings", with "Potential Rating Upgrades" listed as a liability-side positive.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Gold loans (the dominant engine).** AUM INR 19,179 cr, +111% YoY, ~48% of book. Growth "primarily led by healthy customer demand and improving branch productivity" **despite** a gold-price correction. Collateral weight 19 → 20.2 tons (+6% QoQ); active customers +11% QoQ; GNPA 0.3%; yield ~18.5–18.6%; disbursement LTV ~71%. Yield gain is a deliberate **ticket-size** strategy: "we have gone for the smaller ticket size. And accordingly, we change our incentive plan to bring the focus on the smaller ticket size where the yield improvement is possible."
- **MSME / Micro-LAP.** AUM INR 6,779 cr (+24% YoY); disbursements INR 616 cr (+32% YoY). MSME's *share* of AUM has fallen — management is explicit that this was a **capital-allocation choice, not underwriting stress**: "it was primarily because we were opening the new branches in the gold loan and we wanted those branches to achieve profitability for us. So, all the allocation of capital was towards the gold loan segment… we have maintained measured growth in the MSME segment." Micro-LAP AUM INR 876 cr, with tightened screening — "implementation of a **BRE and Bureau score card criteria** to disqualify non-eligible customers upfront."
- **Housing finance (Capri Global Housing Finance).** AUM INR 7,815 cr (+42% YoY); CAR 27.8%. Yields improving via mix — self-employed "now comprises about **75% of AUM**." South-India build (30+ branches) at INR 65 cr/month disbursement. Subsidiary crossed INR 5,000 cr AUM, which under RBI regulation forced a **separate CCO and CFO** — the source of several leadership "transitions" (see §11).
- **Construction finance.** AUM INR 6,332 cr (+40% YoY); 291 projects; avg sanction ticket INR 41 cr vs outstanding ticket INR 20 cr. "granular, secured and well diversified by geography… midsized developers in metro and Tier 1 cities," with "rigorous due diligence and **escrow-based cash flow management**." Recovery playbook stated explicitly: "within **6 to 9 months**, we are able to recover these accounts, which are backed by strong collateral. Further, we find some other project developer to take over the project and recover the amount."
- **Co-lending + Direct Assignment.** AUM INR 8,126 cr (+74% YoY, +4% QoQ), 20% of AUM; income INR 65 cr (−8% YoY). **11 partners, 6 banks already on CLM1**; "We have completed tech integration for new arrangements with CLM1, and we are in the process of migrating other partner banks as well." Workaround in flight: "we are also leveraging **direct assignment and PTC instrument**, which is showing a good demand given higher share of gold loan and the **PSL nature** of our loan book."
- **Insurance distribution — Capri Care.** Net fee income INR 42 cr in the quarter; **14 life and general insurance products launched** with leading insurers; open-market platform expanded via a growing **POSP network** reaching "beyond the lending ecosystem." Forward plan: cross-sell retail health and motor insurance digitally.
- **Car-loan distribution.** Origination INR 3,282 cr (+43% YoY), 13 partner banks. Model is lead-sourcing through employees + dealer network passed to banks via a technology platform.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Compounding data advantage from scale of interactions (management's own framing, with numbers attached).** "Together, this creates a continuous expanding data ecosystem where every transaction and every field interaction feeds back into AI models… creating a compounding technology advantage that strengthens with every customer interaction," and "because each of these systems improve as it processes more transactions, the advantage compounds with scale, making our technology platform an increasingly meaningfully competitive differentiator for the business." Evidenced by 6.7 lakh calls + 2.64 lakh geo-tagged visits + ~70mn monthly API transactions — i.e. a volume-fed rather than asserted claim.
- **Physical intelligence layer competitors mostly lack.** "Over 2.64 lakh **geo-tagged field visits** were recorded… Every visit is digitally verified with a location stamp, creating high-quality field intelligence that strengthens fraud detection and provide a **more comprehensive view on borrowers' behaviour than digital interaction alone**."
- **Vintage-driven operating leverage as a structural cost edge.** Holding gold branches flat at 1,000 for a quarter lifted productivity to INR 19 cr/branch from INR 17 cr, and employee productivity to INR 3.4 cr AUM/employee from INR 1.8 cr on a **14% YoY** headcount increase — with cost-to-income falling 44.2% from 49.4%. Management attributes it to "the benefit of investment in technology, vintaging branch network, rising productivity and improving operational leverage."
- **Automated LTV/margin-call discipline as the gold-book moat.** "the gold loan prices do not fall at single point of time; it could be 10%, 15%, 20% for which there is a set **automated system-driven margin call alert**. And then at some point of time when **LTV breaches beyond level of 85%, the auction notices are issued**." The claimed proof: gold GNPA 0.3% through a quarter of falling gold prices.
- **Collateralisation as the credit-cost floor.** "since we are into **100% collateralized secured segments**… we have built a strong collection culture in the company. So, we believe that there will be not much surprise on the collection side" — with a 525+ own collection team rather than outsourced recovery.
- **PSL-nature of the book as a funding/off-load advantage.** Direct assignment and PTC "showing a good demand given **higher share of gold loan and the PSL nature** of our loan book" — a structural buyer base that non-PSL NBFC books do not have.
business.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position

business.body:
> Only challenges management **specifically raised on THIS call**. Names resolved against `output/concall/companies.csv` (✅) first, then `shadow_paths.load_stock_metadata()` for codes; ⭐ = sector knowledge with code verified vs metadata. **No public/web sources used.** Where nothing resolves from our own files, the cell is left **unmapped** rather than guessed.

| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Gold-price correction hitting LTV:** "gold prices have been on the lower side. And quarter-on-quarter basis, we have seen a **4% decline** in the price, and that has resulted in more Stage 2 cases"; "**The further fall in the gold prices might affect a growth**" | Gold lenders with low disbursal LTV + automated margin-call/auction discipline: **CGCL** (this note; LTV ~71%, auction at 85%, gold GNPA 0.3%) · **MUTHOOTFIN** ⭐ (533398 · NBFC) · **MANAPPURAM** ⭐ (531213 · NBFC) · **FEDFINA** ✅ (544027 · gold loans + LAP NBFC) · **CSBBANK** ⭐ (542867 · Private Sector Bank, gold-led) | High-LTV / aggressive-tenor gold books and banks with gold-led RAM growth taking the same mark-to-market: **KARURVYSYA** ✅ (590003 · gold-loan-led old private bank) · **SOUTHBANK** ✅ (532218 · gold-loan-led private bank) · **IIFL** ⭐ (532636 · NBFC, gold) | **Med-High.** Management quantifies the price move (4% QoQ) and the exact Stage-2 consequence (INR 373 cr of a INR 385 cr rise). The differentiator is disbursal LTV and auction automation, both of which CGCL states verbatim; the read-through applies to any gold book on the same collateral. |
| **New co-lending guidelines / forced CLM1 migration:** "Co-lending volume slowed down during the quarter to 4% growth quarter-on-quarter on account of **new co-lending guidelines** coming into effect and requirement of partner banks to **move to CLM1 model**. Of our 11 partners, **6 banks have already moved to CLM1 model**" | Originators already tech-integrated for CLM1 and able to pivot to DA/PTC on a PSL-eligible book: **CGCL** ("We have completed tech integration for new arrangements with CLM1") · **NORTHARC** ✅ (544260 · diversified NBFC / credit platform, securitization & credit-solutions) · **FEDFINA** ✅ (544027 · co-lending NBFC) | Originators structurally dependent on co-lending flow with partner banks still un-migrated: **Apollo Finvest (India)** ✅ (BSE 512437 · digital/co-lending NBFC) · **MOBIKWIK** ✅ (544305 · digital lending via NBFC co-lending) · **CGCL** itself on the income line (co-lending & DA income INR 65 cr, **−8% YoY**) | **High.** This is a regulation with a hard, already-visible P&L effect (income −8% YoY on 20% of AUM) and an explicit migration count (6 of 11). The winner/loser split is simply who finished the integration first. |
| **Monsoon strength suppresses gold-loan demand:** "if the monsoon is weaker, some of the **micro finance and marginal farmer** will go for the requirement to meet their cash gaps by way of acquiring gold loans" (i.e. a *good* monsoon removes that need) | A strong monsoon relieves rural repayment stress for JLG/rural lenders: **SATIN** ✅ (539404 · microfinance-led rural NBFC) · **UJJIVANSFB** ✅ (542904 · SFB, MFI-origin) · **UTKARSHBNK** ✅ (543942 · SFB, MFI-led) · **CREDITACC** ⭐ (541770 · Microfinance Institutions) · **SPANDANA** ⭐ (542759) · **FUSION** ⭐ (543652) | Gold lenders relying on distress-driven rural cash-gap demand: **CGCL** · **MUTHOOTFIN** ⭐ (533398) · **MANAPPURAM** ⭐ (531213) | **Med.** Management stated the mechanism explicitly but immediately capped its own downside — "in any case… on a stable basis, gold loan growing at 25% is absolutely possible." Directionally clear, unquantified. |
| **Cost of funds has stopped falling:** "**FY27, we don't see much scope in the cost of fund reduction from this level**… costs will remain more or less stable during the remaining quarters" | Lenders with asset-side pricing power to offset a flat liability cost — high-yield secured segments: **CGCL** (gold yield +50–75 bps guided; spread guided 7.8%→~8%) · **MUTHOOTFIN** ⭐ (533398) · **MANAPPURAM** ⭐ (531213) · **FIVESTAR** ⭐ (543663 · NBFC, high-yield small-business secured) | Spread-takers that cannot reprice assets and were relying on falling funding costs: **SAMMAANCAP** ✅ (535789 · HFC, "cost-of-funds-led NIM expansion" is its stated thesis) · **CANFINHOME** ✅ (511196 · prime/near-prime HFC) · **LICHSGFIN** ⭐ (500253 · Housing Finance Company) | **Med-High.** CGCL closing the door on further CoF relief for the whole of FY27 is a sector-wide statement about the rate cycle from a lender that added 5 new lenders and INR 3,868 cr of sanctions this quarter — i.e. it is not a franchise-specific funding problem. |
| **Construction-finance single-account slippage and project takeover:** "there is **one particular account that has slipped in the NPA**, and we have also taken the provision of about 70%"; recovery route = "we find **some other project developer to take over the project** and recover the amount" | Developers/platforms that acquire stressed or stalled residential projects: **IBULLSLTD** ✅ (533520 · Real Estate Development & **Distressed Asset Resolution**) | Mid-sized developers in metro/Tier-1 cities dependent on NBFC construction finance — the borrower cohort CGCL names as its own ("working with **midsized developers in metro and Tier 1 cities**"); no individual listed name resolves from our files, so left **unmapped** | **Low-Med.** The takeover mechanism is stated verbatim and repeatedly ("we have shown repeatedly in the past in many occasions"), but management named no counterparty. Only IBULLSLTD resolves from our own files on a distressed-resolution mandate; the loser side is deliberately left unmapped. |
| **Cash-burn competition in car-loan distribution:** "There are **some players who do the cash burn and grow their volume**, but we are following a philosophy not to do the cash burn. And every transaction should result in some profitability" | Distribution platforms run on unit economics with bank/FI partner rails: **CGCL** (13 partner banks, INR 3,282 cr origination +43% YoY) · **TURTLEMINT** ⭐ (544799 · Fintech — tech-enabled adviser/PoSP-led distribution) | Volume-chasing digital loan marketplaces funding growth with cash burn — management named none, and no such listed name resolves from `companies.csv` / `products.csv`; left **unmapped** | **Low.** Management made the accusation generically and refused to name anyone; the beneficiary side is a business-model read, not a company-specific claim. |
| **Micro-LAP borrower quality requiring upfront screening:** "we implemented **higher threshold for sourcing and selection of customers** leveraging our data science capabilities, for example, implementation of a **BRE and Bureau score card criteria** to disqualify non-eligible customers upfront" | Lenders with in-house data-science/BRE underwriting depth in small-ticket secured MSME: **CGCL** · **NORTHARC** ✅ (544260 · credit platform with underwriting/analytics stack) · **UGROCAP** ⭐ (511742 · NBFC, data-led MSME lending) | Small-ticket MSME/micro-LAP lenders underwriting on manual or thin-file processes — no specific listed name resolves from our own files; left **unmapped** | **Low-Med.** The tightening is stated as a *preventive* action; management reported no Micro-LAP delinquency deterioration this quarter, so this is a leading indicator of segment stress rather than evidence of it. |

---
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Retail, secured and granular by design: "Retail secured lending has massive under penetration and large credit gap; Retail NBFCs better placed; >85% Retail and 100% Secured loan book; 17.0% Yields, 7.8% Spread and 9.7% NIM for Q1 FY27", catering to unbanked/underserved self-employed and salaried customers in semi-urban and rural Tier 2/3/4 cities.
- Scale at Q1 FY27: ₹401bn AUM, 1,433 branches, 21 States & UTs, 13,931 employees, 765K+ customers, 40+ lenders and 11+ co-lending partners. The deck states the AUM growth rate three different ways — "62% CAGR (FY22-FY26)" (at-a-glance), "52.8% AUM CAGR from 2022-Q1FY27" (summary highlights, also the journey chart's "CAGR 52.8%") and "Consolidated AUM Up 53% CAGR FY22-Q1FY27" (AUM slide header).
- Stated differentiators for the "aspiring" and T2/T3 segment: high-touch model with strong customer ownership, specialised underwriting of informal income and SORP/SOCP collateral, understanding of micro-markets, rural reach beyond banks' current customer segment, and a technology-first model to lower TAT.
- Execution record: "Launched, built and scaled 4 new products in last 5 years – Lending - Gold Loans, Micro Lap, Fee Income - Car Loan Origination, Insurance Distribution"; in gold the deck claims "fastest amongst peers to reach average AUM per branch of INR 192 million within ~4 years of launch".
- Market opportunity framing: slide headline is "Capri Global's Focus Segments Present a ₹26tn Opportunity", while the same slide lists FY2026 segment market sizes of MSME ₹51tn, Housing ₹42tn (home loans market size), Gold ₹41tn and Construction Finance ₹16tn; the relationship between the ₹26tn headline and these segment sizes is not explained in the extract.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Ownership] Shareholding as at end-June'26: Promoter Group 59.9%, Institutional Shareholders 26.6%, Other Public Shareholders 13.5%; market capitalisation ₹219bn / US$2.3bn (NSE, 30th June 2026, at USD/INR 95), paid-up equity ₹962.2mn, face value ₹1.

Ltd., Capri Global Securities Pvt. Ltd. and Capri Global Insurance Brokers Pvt. Ltd. "were also incorporated in 2025".
- [Board] Chairman & Independent Director is Lingam Venkata Prabhakar (ex-MD & CEO Canara Bank, ex-ED Punjab National Bank); Rajesh Sharma is Promoter & Managing Director with over 3 decades in financial services; the board has 5 independent directors with banking, finance, risk, IT and public-policy expertise.

business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- **Spread at 7.8%, yield 17%** — "driven by increasing share of high-yield products, increase in our gold loan yields and improvement in costs of borrowing." Guided to hold: "in the range of about 7.8% and maybe around 8%… when gold loan proportion cross 50%, 53%."
- **Yield expansion is a mix + ticket-size decision, not repricing.** Smaller-ticket gold focus plus an amended incentive plan; a further 50–75 bps guided for next quarter.
- **Cost of funds fell only ~10 bps in the quarter** (analyst's figure, unchallenged) and management explicitly closed the door on more: "FY27, we don't see much scope in the cost of fund reduction from this level… costs will remain more or less stable during the remaining quarters." Improvement so far came from "active effort of repricing existing borrowings, **MCLR reduction** and optimizing ALM through changing mix."
- **Funding diversification substitutes for price.** Public bond issuance, commercial paper, institutional refinancing, higher bank borrowings and the USD 1bn GMTN — "we'll ensure that the overall share of bank borrowing percentage declines." NCD + CP now ~10% of the mix.
- **Cost-to-income 44.2% vs 49.4% QoQ** with opex flat QoQ and only 156 net employee adds "on account of branch optimization." But the improvement is guided to stop: "over next 12 to 18 months, cost-to-income ratio should remain in this range. **It will not go further down**, keeping in mind that we are going to add more branches. And more branch expenses will get offset by large volumes from the old branches."
- **ALM is favourably positioned:** "Our liabilities are long tenure and our assets are short to medium tenure… with cumulative surplus across all buckets."
- **Credit cost anchored:** impairment INR 62 cr = 0.7% of average total assets, "in line with our historical average of 0.6% to 0.8%."

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** First note on CGCL. Consolidated AUM **INR 40,112 cr (+62% YoY, +10% QoQ)**; gold loan AUM **INR 19,179 cr (+111% YoY)**, ~48% of book; MSME **INR 6,779 cr (+24%)**; housing **INR 7,815 cr (+42%)**; construction finance **INR 6,332 cr (+40%)**; disbursements **INR 11,114 cr (+31%)**. NII **INR 736 cr (+79%)**; non-interest income **INR 217 cr (+28%)**; PPOP **INR 532 cr (+71%)**; **PAT INR 353 cr (+102% YoY), highest ever**. ROAE **19.1%** (vs 13%), ROAA **4.1%** (vs 3.2%); yield **17%**, spread **7.8%**; cost-to-income **44.2%** (vs 49.4% QoQ). Asset quality: GS3 **1.1%** / NS3 **0.6%**; **Stage 2 rose to 3.8% from 2.8%**, INR 373 cr of the INR 385 cr increase in gold on a 4% QoQ gold-price fall; construction-finance GNPA **0.3%→0.7%** on one account (70% provision); **INR 125 cr under DCCO extension outside GNPA**; CF PCR **70%**, consolidated PCR **43.3%**. Leverage **3.7x**; CAR **24.7%** (NBFC) / **27.8%** (HFC); liquidity **INR 4,037 cr**. **Guidance revised UP**: FY27 AUM INR 47,000 cr → **INR 50,000 cr**; new **FY28 target INR 65,000 cr at 30%+ CAGR**; FY28 ROAE 19–21% / ROAA 4.2–4.7%; branch target revised up to **400 branches "on or before December 2026"** (~150 in Q2, 250 in Q3) after a deliberate zero-add Q1 at 1,000 gold branches. Cost of funds and cost-to-income both guided to stop improving. Co-lending/DA AUM INR 8,126 cr (+74% YoY) but **income INR 65 cr, −8% YoY** on the CLM1 transition (6 of 11 partners migrated). New: **OpenAI collaboration** (exploratory), **USD 1bn GMTN programme**, Nayanthara brand ambassador for South India.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (a) did the ~150-branch Q2 leg land, and is the 400-by-December-2026 commitment still "on track"; (b) did gold-loan yield add the guided **50–75 bps**; (c) does the gold **Stage-2 pool drain back** as prices move, or convert to Stage 3 — and is Stage-2 coverage (11.8%→9.4%) explained this time; (d) how many of the remaining **5 of 11 co-lending partners** migrated to CLM1, and did co-lending/DA income return to YoY growth; (e) spread held at 7.8% and cost-to-income at 44–45% with the branch build under way; (f) gold-mix trajectory toward the guided ~55%; (g) construction-finance GNPA after the one-account slippage and whether the INR 125 cr DCCO exposure moved; (h) quarterly AUM add against the INR 3,000–3,500 cr cadence toward INR 50,000 cr FY27; (i) MSME Telangana/Karnataka 16 branches live from Q3; (j) any progress from "we will explore" to deployment on the OpenAI tie-up._

outlook.body:
- **AUM — revised UPWARD, twice on the call.** Opening: "confident of revising our AUM target to **INR65,000 crores by FY28**." Closing: "glad to revise our AUM guidance upwards to **INR65,000 crores by FY28 with 30% plus CAGR**." Prior FY28 anchor did not exist; the **prior FY27 target of INR 47,000 cr is now INR 50,000 cr** — "for FY27, we are on course to achieve INR50,000 crores and by FY28, INR65,000 crores."
- **Quarterly AUM cadence:** "on a quarterly basis, it can be in the range of about **INR3,000 to INR3,500** [crores]. However, the last 2 quarters are always higher on momentum than the first 2 quarters."
- **Return ratios:** "consistent **return on average equity of 19% to 21%** and return on average asset about **4.2% to 4.7%**" — timeline pinned on direct question: "**By FY28.** I think we are quite confident to deliver this on a consistent basis despite remaining on the expansion phase with 400 to 500 branch openings a year."
- **Branch rollout — target REVISED UPWARD and hard-dated:** "our rollout plan will be in the quarter 2 about **150 branches**. And then by balance Q3 we will add another **250 branches**. So total **400 branches**, which should be up and running by Q3." And explicitly: "now we have revised target upward to 400 branches, and that will be completed **on or before December 2026**." Opening remarks give the same Q2 leg: "we expect to add **150-plus branches by end of Q2**."
- **MSME geography:** "expanding our footprint into **Telangana and Karnataka with 16 branches scheduled to become operational from Q3** of this year."
- **Gold-loan yield:** "next quarter also, we'll see some improvement in the yield… I think another **50 to 75 basis** further improvement will happen in the yield."
- **Gold-loan mix:** "in the medium term, gold loan in the overall AUM mix should be about **55%**" (currently ~48%).
- **Gold-loan organic growth:** "on a stable basis, gold loan growing at **25%** is absolutely possible" from existing branches, "assuming that there's no growth in the gold loan prices, plus the new addition of the branches will further add to this."
- **Spread:** "a spread will remain in this region only; in the range of about **7.8%** and maybe around **8%** at some point of time when gold loan proportion cross 50%, 53%."
- **Cost of funds — explicitly capped:** "**FY27, we don't see much scope in the cost of fund reduction from this level**… costs will remain more or less stable during the remaining quarters." Diversification, not price, is the lever.
- **Cost-to-income:** "over next **12 to 18 months**, cost-to-income ratio should remain in this range. It will not go further down… if maintained at **44%-45%** I think this is good achievement."
- **Asset quality:** "Our current gross NPA are about **1.1%** and net NPA is about **0.6%**… **We don't see any reduction from here.**" (i.e. no further improvement guided; industry benchmark cited as GNPA ~2% / NNPA 1%.)
- **New product:** "at some point of time, we are going to launch the **used car loan product** also as a pilot and then gradually full-fledged" — undated.
- **Offshore funding:** "at some point of time, depending upon the market conditions, we will also have a established **GMTN program**, so we can access the offshore dollar bond market" — undated.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Disbursements INR 11,114 crores, +31% YoY**, "on account of growing customer base and widening distribution networks"; customer base now **>7.6 lakhs**.
- **The pipeline IS the branch pipeline.** Gold branches held flat at 1,000 in Q1 by design — "allowing those branches to mature and contribute to productivity" after 89 adds in Q4 and 196 in FY26 — and productivity duly rose to INR 19 cr/branch from INR 17 cr. The next leg is 150 branches in Q2 + 250 in Q3.
- **MSME new-geography ramp is already producing:** "Our MSME branches that opened in **Uttar Pradesh in Q3 FY26** are scaling up well and have started delivering **INR18 crores to INR20 crores disbursement per month**." Telangana/Karnataka (16 branches) go live from Q3 FY27.
- **Housing South-India ramp:** "expansion into high potential Southern India states such as Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka with **30-plus branches in the last quarter** is showing good traction with disbursement volume scaling up to **INR65 crores per month**."
- **Construction finance:** 291 active projects, "midsized developers in metro and Tier 1 cities," escrow-based cash-flow management.
- **Car-loan distribution:** INR 3,282 cr origination (+43% YoY) across 13 partner banks — "a scalable platform with pan-India network, which has potential to monetize further for distribution of other products."
- **Liability pipeline:** INR 3,868 cr incremental sanction limits in the quarter; 5 new lender relationships (40+ total); GMTN programme established for **USD 1 billion** global medium-term notes.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline (disbursement pipeline / growth drivers)

outlook.body:
- **AI as a measured operating layer — the most concrete disclosure on the call.** "4 quarters ago, AI at Capri was about building capability, today, it is delivering measurable business outcomes." Named metrics: **6.7 lakh customer calls analysed** in the quarter ("every customer interaction is analysed by AI, not merely sampled"); **2.64 lakh geo-tagged field visits**; **Kronos 4.0** self-learning collections engine deployed "across the entire collection portfolio"; in-house omnichannel throughput up **more than threefold, 166 → 529 messages per minute**, cutting campaign execution time **53%**; "In the first 12 days of June alone, the platform reached over **1.3 lakh customers with a 95.5% delivery rate**"; a multilingual AI voice platform across **9 Indian languages**; and an API-first microservices layer "processing nearly **70 million actionable API transaction every month**." Collections outcome: "**Nearly 90% of inbound payments** across the organizations are digital with MSME and housing finance **exceeding 93%**," and "approximately **35% of collection** across the MSME and housing finance verticals are now managed through technology-enabled solutions."
- **OpenAI collaboration (announced this quarter).** "we have now collaborated with **OpenAI** to bring enterprise-grade generative AI across key business functions… and build an **AI-native lending institution**." Status is explicitly exploratory: "as part of collaboration with OpenAI, **over the coming months, we will explore** the implementation of secured AI-powered deployments and workflow tools to enhance customer service, knowledge management and the operational processes across its branch network."
- **GMTN programme — USD 1 billion.** "establishing our first GMTN program for **USD1 billion** global medium-term note, which will enable diversified borrowing mix, going forward." Access is market-timing dependent and undated.
- **Used-car loan product** — pilot then full launch, undated: "at some point of time, we are going to launch the used car loan product also as a pilot."
- **Insurance fee income scale-up** — POSP open-market distribution beyond the lending base, plus retail health/motor cross-sell; "expected to drive higher insurance penetration and meaningfully enhance fee income contribution over time."
- **Car-loan platform monetisation** — the 13-bank pan-India distribution rail is positioned as reusable "for distribution of other products."
- **Brand/geography push:** "to strengthen our brand presence and to support our expansion plan in South India, we have now collaborated with renowned actor **Nayanthara** as our brand ambassador."

deepdive.thesis: The gold-loan engine has taken over the company: gold is now ~48% of a INR 40,112 cr AUM book (+62% YoY) after growing **111% YoY**, and it is dragging every other line with it — blended yield 17%, spread 7.8%, cost-to-income down to 44.2% from 49.4%, and a **highest-ever quarterly PAT of INR 353 cr, +102% YoY**, with ROAE 19.1% (vs 13%) and ROAA 4.1% (vs 3.2%). Management responded by **revising guidance upward** — FY27 AUM "on course to achieve INR50,000 crores" (vs an earlier INR 47,000 cr target) and a new **INR 65,000 cr FY28 target at 30%+ CAGR** — while committing to a **400-branch build completed "on or before December 2026."** The two things to hold against that: gold's Stage-2 pool jumped INR 373 cr on a 4% QoQ gold-price decline (total Stage 2 ratio 2.8% → 3.8%), and co-lending — 20% of AUM and a pillar of the capital-efficient story — stalled to +4% QoQ with income *down 8% YoY* as the new co-lending guidelines force partner banks onto CLM1.

open.item: New co-lending guidelines (from 1 Jan 2026) may cause a temporary slowdown for a couple of quarters; full volume expected from Sept quarter (Q2FY27), offset by DA.
Plan international bond issuance to diversify borrowing once hedging costs settle (2-4 months); international ratings obtained (Fitch BB-, Moody's Ba3).
Expect a further credit rating upgrade in next 6-9 months, adding ~20 bps cost-of-fund benefit.
FY27 aim ROA about 4% and ROE not less than 16%.
New fixed income/bond vertical expected net fee income INR20-25 crore (gross INR40-50 crore), license expected by end-June; reduces treasury negative carry.
Insurance income to grow in line with AUM at ~25-30%; car loan income ~12-15%; co-lending income roughly flat (offset by DA).
Car loan origination expected to grow 12% to 15% year-on-year, focus shifting to margins.
Adding used car loan distribution this year; car loan entity to deliver ~INR20 crore profit next year, targeting INR60-70 crore fee income over 4-5 years.
Expect about 10-20 bps cost of funds reduction this year, exit ~9%; another 20 bps possible on rating upgrade.
Plan to add ~350 gold loan branches this year (all operational within FY27), 700-800 total incl gold over 2 years.
PAT guidance for FY27 at about INR1,300 crore.
Guidance of about INR46,000 crore AUM by end of FY27.
Targeting ROA between 4.25% to 4.5% and ROE around 16% for upcoming year.
FY27 profit expected in the range of about INR1,200 crore.
FY27 AUM expected in the range of about INR42,000 crore.
FY27 ROAA about 4% and ROAE in range of 16% to 17%.
Sustainable ROE 16-18% and ROA 4-4.5% by FY28.
Over next 18-24 months plan to increase DA/co-lending and raise Tier 2 capital to shore up capital base.
MSME to grow ~20-25%, construction finance ~25-30%, housing ~25-30%, gold ~25-30%.
Targeting overall growth conservatively 25% (25-30% range) with gold growing higher.

verdicts.item: Targeting INR300 billion (INR30,000 crore) consolidated AUM by FY27.
verdicts.note: 'consolidated AUM stood at INR36,623 crores' - already surpasses the INR30,000cr FY27 target a year early.

verdicts.item: Will approach rating agency now that annual results are out; rating upgrade would lower cost of funds.
verdicts.note: First global ratings obtained, but the COF-lowering upgrade still pending ('the credit rating happens in the next 6 to 9 months').

verdicts.item: Overall cost of funds expected to come down by at least 40-50 bps by end of the year.
verdicts.note: COF declined to a ~9-9.1% exit (from ~9.5-9.6%); 'cost of borrowings declined further by 18 bps quarter-on-quarter' - ~40-50bps reduction over FY26.

verdicts.item: Gross NPA will never cross 2% and net NPA will never cross 1.2%.
verdicts.note: 'gross Stage 3 ratio improved further to 0.9%... net Stage 3 ratio stood at 0.5%' - well within the <2% / <1.2% ceilings.

verdicts.item: Expect cost-to-income ratio to remain in range of about 50% for FY26 (46-47% ex-new branches).
verdicts.note: 'cost-to-income ratio for the year has compressed to 49% from 60% a year earlier' - within the ~50% FY26 guide.

verdicts.item: Confident of FY26 ROAE ~13.5-14% and ROAA not less than 3.5%.
verdicts.note: 'return on average equity at 16.5%... return on average assets at 3.5% for the year' - ROAE beats 13.5-14%, ROAA meets >=3.5%.

verdicts.item: Remain on course for ~30% AUM growth this year; do not intend to exceed it.
verdicts.note: FY26 AUM +60% YoY - 30% growth target comfortably met/exceeded.

verdicts.item: New RBI draft LTV norms (interest accrual in LTV) seen as positive/manageable given short 4-6 month gold loan tenure.
verdicts.note: New guidelines (interest accrual in LTV) being implemented; 'there could be a temporary slowdown in co-lending volume for a couple of quarters, but eventually, volume should come back' - manageable bu…

verdicts.item: Gold loan yield (~22%) expected to remain around that level in near future with no sharp decline.
verdicts.note: 'our yields on gold loan have again dropped sequentially by 90 bps... we lowered the yield' via co-lending - contradicts the '~22%, no sharp decline' commitment. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Construction finance to remain at conservative level, not more than 20% of book.
verdicts.note: CF INR5,708cr of INR36,623cr AUM (~16%) - below 20%. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Comfortable leverage at ~3.5x debt-to-equity; will not go above 4x.
verdicts.note: 'low leverage ratio of 3.3x' - within the <=4x limit.

verdicts.item: Plan to add 200-250 branches this year (~100 gold, rest housing/MSME) and 700-800 over 3 years.
verdicts.note: 'net addition of... 318 branches during the year' - exceeds the 200-250 FY26 plan.
